title: Blueprint for the Completion of the Rolen SPT Formalization

nodes.title: E1: Andrews congruence at 5
nodes.statement_latex: $\mathsf{Andrews}_5$ is the proposition $5\mid\spt(5k+4)$ for every $k\ge0$.

nodes.title: E1: Andrews congruence at 7
nodes.statement_latex: $\mathsf{Andrews}_7$ is the proposition $7\mid\spt(7k+5)$ for every $k\ge0$.

nodes.title: E1: Andrews congruence at 13
nodes.statement_latex: $\mathsf{Andrews}_{13}$ is the proposition $13\mid\spt(13k+6)$ for every $k\ge0$.

nodes.title: E2: Ahlgren--Kim finite exclusion
nodes.statement_latex: $\mathsf{AK}_{\rm fin}$ is Ahlgren--Kim Theorem 3 with its published range and normalizations.

nodes.title: E2: Ahlgren--Kim theta-cycle theorem
nodes.statement_latex: $\mathsf{AK}_{\Theta}$ is the correctly normalized implication of Ahlgren--Kim Proposition 6, before eta cancellation or coefficient extraction.

nodes.title: E3: Bringmann completion and shadow
nodes.statement_latex: $\mathsf{Bringmann}$ is the exact published existence theorem for the harmonic Maass completion of $f$, including its holomorphic part and normalized eta shadow.

nodes.title: E3: Hecke--shadow intertwining
nodes.statement_latex: $\mathsf{ShadowHecke}$ is the general dual-weight Hecke/shadow identity from the cited harmonic-Maass-form theory, including its scalar factors.

nodes.title: E4: Dedekind eta foundations
nodes.statement_latex: $\mathsf{EtaFoundations}$ is the standard transformation law, nonvanishing on the upper half-plane, and integral unit product expansion of Dedekind's eta function, with the exact multiplier convention.

nodes.title: E4: Euler eta component-theta identity
nodes.statement_latex:
$\mathsf{EtaTheta}$ is Euler's standard componentwise theta identity
$\sum_{r\bmod 12}\chi_{12}(r)\theta_r=2\eta$ in a complex series
realization.  It contains no Atkin--Lehner, cusp-pairing, or Weyl-vector
conclusion.

nodes.title: E4: modular invariant foundations
nodes.statement_latex: $\mathsf{JFoundations}$ is the standard modularity and integral Fourier expansion $j=q^{-1}+744+\cdots$ of the modular invariant.

nodes.title: E4: Eisenstein-series foundations
nodes.statement_latex: $\mathsf{EisensteinFoundations}$ gives the exact weights, transformation laws, and integral Fourier expansions of $E_4$ and $E_6$.

nodes.title: E4: principal-part integrality
nodes.statement_latex: $\mathsf{PrincipalIntegral}$ is the standard theorem that a qualified weakly holomorphic form with integral principal part has integral Fourier expansion in the stated lattice.

nodes.title: E4: general modular Hecke laws
nodes.statement_latex: $\mathsf{ModHecke}$ is the general Hecke law for the relevant weakly holomorphic weights and multipliers, with no Rolen-specific identity as its conclusion.

nodes.title: E3/E4: source Hecke qualifications
nodes.statement_latex:
$\mathsf{I05Qual}(G)$ is the exact citation-level assertion, obtained from the
published completion/shadow and general modular Hecke laws, that the concrete
normalized left side of the $f$ identity qualifies in the grid space at index
$p$, and that the concrete normalized left side of the grid recurrence
qualifies at index $mp$, throughout the source-valid range.  It contains no
principal-part assertion and neither desired Hecke identity.

nodes.title: E4: weight-two residue theorem
nodes.statement_latex: $\mathsf{Residue}_2$ is the standard theorem that a weakly holomorphic weight-two form on the relevant compact modular curve has zero constant term.

nodes.title: E4: published mock modular grid theorem
nodes.statement_latex: $\mathsf{AKGrid}$ is the exact Ahlgren--Kim mock modular grid theorem, only if its published multiplier, normalization, coprime range, principal parts, and uniqueness statement match the grid used here.  It contains no theta-support or coefficient-duality conclusion.

nodes.title: E5: Bruinier--Ono general lift
nodes.statement_latex: $\mathsf{BO}$ is Bruinier--Ono Theorem 6.1 with its original hypotheses and its general product-expansion, character, and Heegner-divisor conclusions; it says nothing about Rolen's particular vector input or class-polynomial quotient.

nodes.title: E6: Bruinier--Schwagenscheidt Weyl formula
nodes.statement_latex: $\mathsf{BS}$ is the general Weyl-vector formula of Bruinier--Schwagenscheidt, equation (11), with the exact cusp and normalization conventions.

nodes.title: E7: Ligozat eta-quotient theorem
nodes.statement_latex: $\mathsf{Ligozat}$ is the general eta-quotient modularity, character, and cusp-order theorem.  It contains no specialized degree-one conclusion for Rolen's $t$.

nodes.title: E7: good integral model of $X_0(6)$
nodes.statement_latex: $\mathsf{IntegralCurve}_6$ is the standard theorem that the compactified $X_0(6)$ has a smooth proper geometrically connected integral model away from $6$.

nodes.title: E7: genus-zero fibers of $X_0(6)$
nodes.statement_latex: $\mathsf{GenusZero}_6$ is the standard theorem that every geometric fiber away from $6$ is a smooth irreducible curve of genus zero.

nodes.title: E7: disjoint cusp sections
nodes.statement_latex: $\mathsf{Cusps}_6$ is the standard theorem that the four cusp sections $0,1/2,1/3,\infty$ are disjoint on the integral model away from $6$.

nodes.title: E4/E11: squarefree-level cusp classification
nodes.statement_latex:
$\mathsf{SquarefreeCusps}$ is the standard general theorem that, for every
nonzero squarefree level $N$, the $\Gamma_0(N)$-orbits on
$\mathbb P^1(\mathbb Q)$ are in bijection with the positive divisors $d\mid
N$, using the conventional representatives $0$ for $d=1$, $1/d$ for the
intermediate divisors, and $\infty$ for $d=N$.

nodes.title: E8: CM ideal-class action
nodes.statement_latex: $\mathsf{CMClassAction}$ is the standard simply transitive proper ideal-class action on CM points of a fixed order and orientation.

nodes.title: E8: CM class counts
nodes.statement_latex: $\mathsf{CMClassCount}$ is the standard equality between the number of proper ideal classes of the order and its class number.

nodes.title: E8/E11: quadratic order is a domain
nodes.statement_latex:
$\mathsf{QuadraticOrderDomain}(n)$ is the standard fact that
$\mathbf Z[(1+\sqrt{-n})/2]$, presented as the concrete quadratic
\texttt{AdjoinRoot}, is a domain when $-n$ is a negative fundamental
discriminant.  It contains no class action or cardinality conclusion.

nodes.title: E8/E11: reduced forms and proper ideal classes
nodes.statement_latex:
$\mathsf{ReducedFormClassification}(n)$ is the standard equivalence, for a
negative fundamental discriminant, between the concrete reduced primitive
positive form classes (with the stated boundary convention) and proper ideal
classes of $\mathbf Z[(1+\sqrt{-n})/2]$.

nodes.title: E8/E11: fixed-orientation form classification
nodes.statement_latex:
$\mathsf{OrientedFormClassification}(n)$ is the standard refinement of the
form--ideal-class correspondence for $n\equiv23\pmod{24}$, after choosing
one prime above each of $2$ and $3$: the proper ideal-class group is equivalent to each of the four
concrete quotients $\mathcal Q_{n,1},\mathcal Q_{n,11},
\mathcal Q_{n,5},\mathcal Q_{n,7}$.  This external input contains no action
and no cardinality conclusion.

nodes.title: E8: potential good reduction with level
nodes.statement_latex: $\mathsf{CMGoodReduction}$ is the standard potential-good-reduction theorem for CM elliptic curves with prime-to-$\ell$ level structure.

nodes.title: E8: Deuring inert reduction
nodes.statement_latex: $\mathsf{Deuring}$ is the theorem that inert reduction of a CM elliptic curve is supersingular.

nodes.title: E8: injectivity of specialized CM action
nodes.statement_latex: $\mathsf{CMSpecialization}$ is injectivity of the relevant CM-order action after the chosen good specialization.

nodes.title: E9: Arpin level-six Eichler order
nodes.statement_latex: $\mathsf{Arpin}_6$ is Arpin's theorem identifying the order preserving a cyclic subgroup of order six as the required level-six Eichler order.

nodes.title: E9: Goren--Lauter Hadamard bound
nodes.statement_latex: $\mathsf{GL}$ is the general Goren--Lauter covolume/Hadamard inequality for four independent quaternionic vectors.

nodes.title: E10: corrected Treviño bound
nodes.statement_latex: $\mathsf{Trevino}$ is the corrected all-prime bound $H\le3.38\ell^{1/4}\log\ell$ for a nonprincipal character constant on $H$ consecutive integers.

nodes.title: E11: binary quadratic-form reduction
nodes.statement_latex: $\mathsf{BQFReduction}$ is the standard reduction theorem for positive definite integral binary quadratic forms, including the boundary convention used in the class count.

nodes.title: E11: quadratic reciprocity
nodes.statement_latex: $\mathsf{Reciprocity}$ is quadratic reciprocity with the exact sign and congruence conventions used for the progression $1-24k$.

nodes.title: E11: Euler criterion
nodes.statement_latex: $\mathsf{EulerCriterion}$ is Euler's criterion and multiplicativity for the Legendre symbol over odd prime fields.

nodes.title: E11: finite-height Stokes theorem
nodes.statement_latex: $\mathsf{Stokes}$ is the general finite-height Stokes identity and limiting theorem for qualified modular inputs.  It contains no value of Rolen's constant term or pairing.

nodes.title: Permitted literature record
nodes.statement_latex: $\mathsf{RolenLiterature}$ is the record whose proof fields are exactly the propositions in E1--E11 above, with their ambient objects and source metadata.

nodes.title: Multiplicity of the smallest part [B
nodes.statement_latex:
]

For a partition $\pi$, $\mu(\pi)$ is the multiplicity of its least part, and is zero for the empty partition.

nodes.title: Smallest-parts function [B
nodes.statement_latex:
]

$\spt(n):=\sum_{\pi\vdash n}\mu(\pi)$.

nodes.title: Canonical residue
nodes.statement_latex: For prime $\ell\ge5$, $b_\ell$ is the unique integer in $[1,\ell)$ satisfying $24b_\ell\equiv1\pmod\ell$.

nodes.title: Canonical congruence prime
nodes.statement_latex: $\Can(\ell)$ means that $\ell$ is prime, $\ell\ge5$, and $\ell\mid\spt(\ell k+b_\ell)$ for every $k\ge0$.

nodes.title: Mock coefficient series
nodes.statement_latex: Let $a(r)$ be the normalized coefficients of $f(\tau)=\sum_r a(r)q^{r/24}$ used by Rolen.

nodes.title: $U_\ell$ on numerator-indexed series
nodes.statement_latex: For a numerator-indexed series $g$, $(g|U_\ell)(r):=g(\ell r)$.

nodes.title: Correct analytic range
nodes.statement_latex:
$\mathsf{AnalyticAdmissible}(\ell,n)$ means that $\ell$ is prime,
$5\le\ell$, and $\Adm(\ell,n)$ holds.  All characteristic-dependent analytic
data below are indexed by a proof of this predicate.

nodes.title: Canonical grid form
nodes.statement_latex: For $m>1$ with $(m,6)=1$, $G_m$ denotes the genuine integral weakly holomorphic form with principal part $q^{-m^2/24}-\chi_{12}(m)q^{-1/24}$; put $G_1=0$.

nodes.title: Auxiliary form
nodes.statement_latex: For $n=24k-1>0$, $H_n:=\eta P_n(j)$, where the monic polynomial $P_n$ is fixed by the triangular principal-part condition.

nodes.title: Admissible pair
nodes.statement_latex:
$\Adm(\ell,n)$ means that $n$ is squarefree, $n\equiv23\pmod{24}$, and
$-n$ is not a square in $\mathbf Z/\ell\mathbf Z$.  For the prime range used
below this is equivalent to $\left(\frac{-n}{\ell}\right)=-1$.

nodes.title: Level-six Hauptmodul
nodes.statement_latex: $t(\tau):=\eta(\tau)^5\eta(3\tau)/(\eta(2\tau)\eta(6\tau)^5)$.

nodes.title: Actual analytic level-six Hauptmodul
nodes.statement_latex: Let $t_{\rm an}$ be the level-six eta quotient formed with Mathlib's actual Dedekind eta function on the upper half-plane.

nodes.title: Dedekind eta Euler unit
nodes.statement_latex:
For $z\in\C$, put
\[
E_\eta(z):=\prod_{n\ge0}\bigl(1-q(z)^{n+1}\bigr),
\]
using Mathlib's convergent infinite product from the definition of Dedekind
eta.

nodes.title: Level-six Hauptmodul Euler unit
nodes.statement_latex:
For $\tau$ in the upper half-plane, put
\[
E_t(\tau):=\frac{E_\eta(\tau)^5E_\eta(3\tau)}
 {E_\eta(2\tau)E_\eta(6\tau)^5}.
\]

nodes.title: I21: analytic Euler-product bridge
nodes.statement_latex:
For every $\tau$ in the upper half-plane,
\[
t_{\rm an}(\tau)=q(\tau)^{-1}E_t(\tau).
\]
nodes.proof_latex:
Unfold Mathlib's definition
$\eta(z)=q_{24}(z)\prod_{n\ge0}(1-q(z)^{n+1})$.  The four fractional
prefactors have net exponent
$5+3-2-30=-24$, hence combine exactly to $q(\tau)^{-1}$.

nodes.title: One level-six formal Euler factor
nodes.statement_latex:
For $m\ge1$, let
\[
F_m(X):=(1-X^m)^5(1-X^{3m})(1-X^{2m})^{-1}(1-X^{6m})^{-5}
\in\Z[[X]],
\]
where the negative powers are Mathlib's integral formal geometric-series
units after substitution.

nodes.title: Stabilized formal Hauptmodul Euler unit
nodes.statement_latex:
Define $E_t^{\rm form}\in\Z[[X]]$ coefficientwise: its coefficient in
degree $d$ is the degree-$d$ coefficient of
$\prod_{m=1}^{d+2}F_m(X)$.

nodes.title: Formal Hauptmodul unit constant coefficient
nodes.statement_latex: The constant coefficient of $E_t^{\rm form}$ is $1$.
nodes.proof_latex:
Every numerator factor and every substituted geometric-series denominator
factor has constant coefficient one, so their finite stabilized product does
as well.

nodes.title: Formal Hauptmodul unit linear coefficient
nodes.statement_latex: The coefficient of $X$ in $E_t^{\rm form}$ is $-5$.
nodes.proof_latex:
All factors except $(1-X)^5$ have their first nonconstant term in degree at
least two.  Thus the linear coefficient is the linear coefficient of
$(1-X)^5$, namely $-5$.

nodes.title: Hauptmodul Laurent series
nodes.statement_latex:
Let $t_q^{\rm form}:=X^{-1}E_t^{\rm form}\in\Z((X))$.  This is the
independently constructed formal Euler-product candidate; no analytic
identification is included in the definition.

nodes.title: I21: formal principal part
nodes.statement_latex:
The formal Euler-product candidate $t_q^{\rm form}$ has principal part
$X^{-1}-5+O(X)$: its coefficient at $-1$ is one, its coefficient at zero is
$-5$, and all coefficients below $-1$ vanish.
nodes.proof_latex:
Shift the coefficients of $E_t^{\rm form}$ down by one and use its verified
constant and linear coefficients.

nodes.title: I21: analytic/formal identification
nodes.statement_latex:
The analytic Euler unit $E_t(\tau)$ is represented on the punctured unit
disk by the coefficientwise stabilized integral series
$E_t^{\rm form}$; consequently $t_{\rm an}$ has Laurent expansion
$t_q^{\rm form}$.
nodes.proof_latex:
This is the remaining analytic/formal bridge: justify convergence of the
substituted formal factors on the unit disk, identify their finite products
with the analytic products, and pass coefficientwise stabilization through
the locally uniform limit.

nodes.title: Oriented form classes
nodes.statement_latex: $\mathcal Q_{n,r}$ is the set of primitive positive binary quadratic forms of discriminant $-n$, modulo $\Gamma_0(6)$, with middle coefficient congruent to $r\pmod{12}$.

nodes.title: Canonical raw CM point
nodes.statement_latex:
For a raw positive form $Q=[a,b,c]$ of discriminant $-n$ with $n>0$, let
$\tau_Q:=(-b+i\sqrt n)/(2a)\in\mathbb H$.

nodes.title: Actual oriented Hauptmodul value
nodes.statement_latex:
Given the transformation-law proof that the actual eta quotient is invariant
under the concrete $\Gamma_0(6)$ relation, $Q\mapsto t(\tau_Q)$ descends along
the equivalence closure to a function on the actual quotient
$\mathcal Q_{n,r}$.

nodes.title: Numerator class polynomial
nodes.statement_latex: $A_n^{\C}(X):=\prod_{r\in\{1,11\}}\prod_{Q\in\mathcal Q_{n,r}}(X-t(\tau_Q))$ is the actual complex numerator root product.  No individual CM root is asserted to lie in $\Z[1/6]$.

nodes.title: Denominator class polynomial
nodes.statement_latex: $B_n^{\C}(X):=\prod_{r\in\{5,7\}}\prod_{Q\in\mathcal Q_{n,r}}(X-t(\tau_Q))$ is the actual complex denominator root product.  No individual CM root is asserted to lie in $\Z[1/6]$.

nodes.title: Coefficientwise reduction
nodes.statement_latex: For $\ell>3$ and a proved $\Z[1/6]$-descent $P$ of the two actual complex root products, $(\bar A_{\ell,n},\bar B_{\ell,n})$ is obtained by reducing the descended coefficients modulo $\ell$.

nodes.title: Wronskian obstruction
nodes.statement_latex: $\Wr(A,B):=A'B-AB'$.

nodes.title: Positive Euler product
nodes.statement_latex: $P_n^+(q)$ is the coefficientwise stabilized product $\prod_{m\ge1}(1-q^m)^{\max(e_n(m),0)}$.

nodes.title: Negative Euler product
nodes.statement_latex: $P_n^-(q)$ is the coefficientwise stabilized product $\prod_{m\ge1}(1-q^m)^{\max(-e_n(m),0)}$.

nodes.title: Reduced auxiliary coefficient form
nodes.statement_latex: For an integral auxiliary coefficient function $H$, let $\bar H_\ell$ be its coefficientwise reduction to $\F_\ell$.

nodes.title: Reduced-form class number
nodes.statement_latex: $h_{\rm red}(-n)$ is the cardinality of the finite type of primitive reduced positive forms of discriminant $-n$.

nodes.title: Genuine-grid specification
nodes.statement_latex:
$\mathsf{GenuineGridSpec}$ consists of the published grid family, its exact
modular qualification predicate, the convention $G_1=0$, its normalized
principal parts for $m>1$ coprime to $6$, and uniqueness with those data.

nodes.title: Hecke-identity specification
nodes.statement_latex:
For a fixed published grid and concrete qualification data $D$ naming the
two sides, $\mathsf{HeckeSpec}(G,D)$ is the property that those sides obey
Rolen's two source-normalized Hecke formulas in their exact valid ranges.

nodes.title: Auxiliary-form specification
nodes.statement_latex: $\mathsf{HnSpec}(n,H)$ records the exact weight, multiplier, integrality, and Fourier normalization required of $H_n$.

nodes.title: Signed-exponent specification
nodes.statement_latex:
$\mathsf{SignedExponentSpec}(H,m)$ records that the natural positive and
negative parts of $e(m)=\chi_{12}(m)H(m^2)$ have difference $e(m)$, are
one-sided, and vanish when $(m,6)>1$.

nodes.title: Laurent Hauptmodul specification
nodes.statement_latex:
$\mathsf{LaurentSpec}(\ell,n,h)$ consists of a Laurent series $t_q$ with
principal part $q^{-1}-5+O(q)$.  In the intended range $h$, the pole proves
transcendence over $\F_\ell$, hence injective polynomial substitution; it also
proves that the formal derivative is nonzero.  These consequences are derived
from the principal part rather than stored as extra fields.

nodes.title: Vector-valued input specification
nodes.statement_latex: $\mathsf{VectorInputSpec}(n,\mathbf H_n)$ records the exact Weil transformation law, zero constant term, and integral principal part required by Bruinier--Ono.

nodes.title: Stabilized-product specification
nodes.statement_latex: $\mathsf{EulerProductSpec}(H,P^+,P^-)$ records coefficientwise stabilization of the two canonical products, unit constant terms, invertibility, and the pointwise positive-minus-negative signed-exponent decomposition.  It contains no Borcherds quotient identity.

nodes.title: Class-polynomial arithmetic specification
nodes.statement_latex: $\mathsf{ClassPolySpec}(n,P)$ is a descent of the two actual complex root products to polynomials $A_n,B_n\in\Z[1/6][X]$, with literal coefficient-map equalities and monicity.  It records no lift of any individual CM root to $\Z[1/6]$.

nodes.title: Algebraic-closure reduction specification
nodes.statement_latex:
$\mathsf{RootReductionSpec}(P,h_6)$ records coefficientwise reduction of
the integral pair $P$ to $\F_\ell[X]$ and the common-root criterion over an
algebraic closure, where $h_6$ certifies that $6$ is invertible.

nodes.title: Class-count specification
nodes.statement_latex:
$\mathsf{ClassCountSpec}(n)$ packages a domain instance for the concrete
quadratic order, equality of the reduced-form count with its ordinary
ideal-class number $h(-n)$, and the cardinality $h(-n)$ of every one of the
four oriented form sets.

nodes.title: Specialized-action specification
nodes.statement_latex:
For a specialized CM pair $S$, $\mathsf{ActionSpec}(S)$ records the two
orientation residues and their scalar actions on the level-six subgroup,
the two trace-one identities, and equality of the two reduced norms.
Noncommutation is not a field of this specification.

nodes.title: Common-root specialization specification
nodes.statement_latex:
For a standard CM model, $\mathsf{CollisionSpec}$ consists of two CM points
with the same reduction, potentially good reduction for both points,
supersingularity of the common reduction, and injectivity of both specialized
CM actions.

nodes.title: Small-discriminant specification
nodes.statement_latex: $\mathsf{SmallDisc}(\ell,n)$ records admissibility, the collision inequality, and the positive degree bound below $\ell$.

nodes.section: Sound analytic interfaces and the grid: I01--I08, I13, I21
nodes.statement_latex:
